newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Tatneft plans Level 3 ADR issue.
newsitem.headline: Tatneft plans Level 3 ADR issue.

text.p: Russian oil company Tatneft said on Wednesday it planned to issue Level Three American Depositary Receipts and was preparing the necessary information.

"The only thing which is holding us back is the need to state accounts to international standards for three years, and 1996 has not finished yet," said Nail Gamirov, head of AO Tatneft's securities department.
He said accountants Price Waterhouse had already audited the firm's 1994 and 1995 results to international standards and that they would be published in early October.
An audit of Tatneft's oil reserves by U.S. petroleum engineers Miller and Lents was expected in the next few days.

Issuing Level Three ADRs amounts to a public offering of securities which are listed on a U.S. exchange. The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission requires detailed disclosure, including three years' accounts to U.S. accounting standards and the process can be costly.

No Russian company has yet issued Level Three ADRs and bankers said it was not clear whether Tatneft really intended to do so or just to raise capital with ADRs -- either through a private placement or a Level Two issue.
Tatneft, like several other Russian companies, has issued Level One ADRs which do not raise new capital.
Tatneft shares, which are not very liquid, were untraded on the Russian Trading System on Wednesday after closing at $27.75 on Tuesday.
Tatneft ADRs were quoted at $24/$28 by Brunswick Brokerage BRRU.
Tatneft's pre-tax profit rose in 1995 to 2.40 trillion roubles from 210.5 billion in 1994, according to Russian accounting standards.
Oil output rose in 1995 to 24.14 million tonnes from 23.0 million in 1994.
The government of the Russian region of Tatarstan holds 41 percent of Tatneft's shares, employees have 41.34 percent and 3.66 percent are held by suppliers.
